newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower, after 5-day rally.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower, after 5-day rally.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended sharply lower Thursday, breaking a five day recovery from multi-month lows.

"We saw a good recovery in the past week, but it was mostly fund short covering and the market ran into trade selling again today, which prompted some funds to sell again also," Pioneer Futures Inc New York trader Scott Meyers said.
"We really need to get up to $387 in December gold to provoke a good rally, but my heart tells me it's not going to happen," he said.
COMEX December gold ended down $2.40 an ounce at $381.80, retreating from a ten day high at $385.80 seen Wednesday.
Estimated gold futures volume was 40,000 lots.
Spot gold ended quoted $381.00/381.40, down from the London Thursday afternoon fix at $383.00 and the New York close Wednesday around $383.05/383.45.
COMEX December silver closed down 5.8 cents at $4.840 an ounce, with total silver futures volume estimated at 18,000 lots.
The spot gold/silver ratio firmed to 78.40, from 78.15 at the close Wednesday, as gold led the way back down.
Spot gold has recovered from 18 month lows at $376.80 on November 1, but the long running downtrend since February this year has not been reversed yet, despite improving fundamentals, analysts said.

Fabrication demand in India saw year-on-year growth of around 10 percent in the first nine months of 1996, while in Germany fabrication demand in the first nine months this year was little changed from last year, and in the U.S. demand looks to about three to six percent higher, CPM Group analyst Jeffrey Christian said.
Meanwhile, South African gold output fell 5.9 pct through September, dropping to 11.83 million ounces.

Total COMEX gold warehouse stocks fell from 1.28 million ounces on October 2 to 1.06 million on October 31, while open interest in the active December gold contract fell from 11.32 million ounces on October 2 to 10.23 million October 31.
But the missing factor is investment demand, analysts said.
With the Dow Jones Industrial Average ending above 6300 for the first time Thursday and bond yields falling, there was little incentive for investors to move into gold.
Investment demand has a 23 pct weighting in CPM Group's econometric model used to account for and forecast price movements in gold.

NYMEX January platinum closed down $2.20 at $389.50 an ounce Thursday, while NYMEX December palladium ended off $3.10 an ounce at $120.50, after seeing its highest level since mid-September Wednesday, following a partial recovery from three year lows for spot palladium.
"The palladium market has been buffeted by rumors of sharply lower electronics use since mid-year," Christian said.
"Some market participants have been focusing on industry data released by the semiconductor industry, indicating a slowdown in that booming sector."
Palladium paste is widely used in the production of semiconductors.
"What is missing is total semiconductor unit sales, which, as it turns out, have actually remained high for most of 1996," he said.
"With the prices of some chips off 80 pct, the market has focussed on the depressed state of the industry, overlooking the fact that unit sales are flat to higher."
-- Clive McKeef, New York Commodities 212-859-1640; email: clive.mckeef@reuter.com
